A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, and central theory. Their complete main texts and appendices A-D, including equations, figures, and tables, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C-D report original image-classification experiments, including prediction-set size, coverage, sensitivity analyses, and similarity ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet evaluation, corruption and calibration-size experiments, trial-level comparisons, and a random-similarity ablation.

M1.justification: The binary out-of-group penalty, embedding-based cosine-similarity penalty, and calibration-based selection of lambda remain unchanged. MA-Random is an additional ablation comparator, not a revision to the proposed MA-CS or MS-CS procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds full 1,000-class ImageNet to the retained CIFAR-100, Living-17, and Mini-ImageNet benchmarks. Appendix C.4 also adds brightness and Gaussian-noise test scenarios on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, expanding evaluation to changed input conditions.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2 adds MA-Random alongside the existing MA-Diag comparator in Tables 10-11, corresponding to v1 Tables 7-8. Standard, Clustered, and AIR remain in the original benchmark comparisons; the ImageNet evaluation extends existing comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds a ViT-B/16 evaluation configuration, a 10% calibration/90% test experiment with RAPS at alpha=0.05, and corruption experiments at alpha=0.1. The original 20%/80% protocol and lambda-selection procedure remain. Section 6.2 now identifies the displayed lambda study as MA-CS, whereas v1's conditional-coverage figure caption identified a model-specific setting; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3-C.4 add analyses of trial-level consistency, sensitivity to reduced calibration data, and robustness to brightness/noise shifts. Appendix D.2 adds random similarities to test whether meaningful class structure matters. Lambda sensitivity and conditional-coverage analyses already existed in v1, although their plotted results are revised.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 random-split trials and report standard deviations for efficiency results. V2 additionally supplies standard deviations for previously mean-only coverage and TopCovGap entries in Tables 3-6, plus per-trial win counts in Appendix C.3. No increase in trial count or new formal significance test is reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for ImageNet, reduced calibration, corruptions, random similarities, and trial consistency. For example, new ImageNet RAPS set sizes at alpha=0.05 are 3.27 for Standard and 2.55 for MS-CS. Retained values also change: Table 4's Clustered-LAC/CIFAR100-RN34 coverage changes from 0.919 to 0.901, and lambda curves are revised. Table 1 swaps SAPS/MA-CS superclass means 1.93 and 1.26 between CIFAR100-RN34 and Living-17, contradicting v2 Table 10.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds the assumption that scores are almost surely distinct to the stated upper coverage bound. The central definitions, Assumptions 1-3, Theorem 4.5, and proofs remain substantively unchanged. Moving three proofs into Appendix A does not add theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central contribution claims remain: class-similarity penalties improve conformal-set coherence and efficiency, with an embedding-based variant requiring no semantic partition. V2's conclusion adds an explicit qualification that gains may diminish for weak classifiers, modestly narrowing the broad applicability claim.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses weak classifiers and dominant groups as failure conditions, the theorem's local scope near zero penalty, and the unresolved extension to continuous MS-CS penalties. Section 5 adds practical guidance about theoretical support, black-box access, and training-data requirements when choosing between variants. These refine the interpretation and limitations of unchanged methods.

D1.justification: Section 6 adds a code-repository link. Appendix D.2 documents that MA-Random retains the similarity-matrix diagonal and uses the existing lambda-tuning procedure. The original training details in Appendix B.1 remain unchanged; the new corruption severities are not specified.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Dosovitskiy et al. for ViT and Hendrycks and Dietterich for corruption experiments, and explicitly contrasts lambda sensitivity with temperature scaling. The main positioning against clustered and hierarchical CP remains. Zhang et al.'s publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: V2 retains the main section sequence and appendix organization while editing the abstract, motivation, discussion, and conclusion. It adds variant-selection guidance and an impact statement, moves three proofs into Appendix A, and relocates the TopCovGap definition to Appendix B.3. Most existing exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ICML layout, expands benchmark and uncertainty tables, and adds three experimental tables and two trial-level figures. Figure 2 becomes a larger two-panel sensitivity display incorporating the earlier appendix analysis; Figure 3's unchanged similarity images are enlarged and stacked. Ablation tables gain MA-Random rows, while the full similarity matrices are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the existing efficiency claim through broader evaluation, meaningful additional controls, and clearer uncertainty reporting, while explaining applicability and theoretical limits more explicitly. These gains are tempered by the new Table 1/Table 10 inconsistency and corruption experiments that omit coverage results and corruption severities. The net improvement is supported but qualified.
